# 17: Personalized College & Major Explorer

**What to build:** Replace the hardcoded `const colleges = [...]` array (and the equivalent static list in `MajorExplorer.tsx`) with real, personalized picks generated by Groq from the student's actual profile. One edge function returns both college and major recommendations in a single call. Auto-triggered on `onboarding_completed` and `career_path_selected` events; a manual "Refresh my picks" button lets the student force a re-pull anytime.

**Blocked by:** 
- Vocabulary extension: add `college` and `major` to `RECOMMENDATION_TYPES` in `lib/constants.ts`, mirrored in the new edge function
- A grounding reference list of real Indian colleges/majors (see Implementation Decisions) — without this the model can hallucinate institutions that don't exist

**Status:** ready-for-agent

- [ ] New edge function (e.g. `generate-explorer-picks`) takes the user's profile + onboarding answers, calls Groq, returns a structured list of college and major recommendations
- [ ] Results are written to `recommendations` with `type: 'college'` / `type: 'major'`, `target_feature: 'explorer'`
- [ ] `CollegeExplorer.tsx` and `MajorExplorer.tsx` render from `recommendationService.getActiveRecommendations(userId, 'explorer')`, filtered by type — not the hardcoded array
- [ ] Completing onboarding triggers generation automatically (student doesn't land on an empty Explorer on day one)
- [ ] Selecting/confirming a career path (wherever that event already fires, or gets added in this ticket) re-triggers generation
- [ ] A visible "Refresh my picks" action re-runs generation on demand
- [ ] The model is grounded against a real reference list of Indian institutions and majors — either passed in the prompt as a candidate pool to rank/select from, or validated against post-generation — so it can't freely invent college names that don't exist
- [ ] Old hardcoded `colleges`/majors arrays are deleted, not left as dead code

## Implementation Decisions

- Grounding approach: simplest viable option is a curated static list (a few hundred well-known Indian colleges across engineering/medical/arts/commerce categories, similarly to how Skill Gap uses a static reference table) passed to Groq as candidates to select and rank from, rather than free generation. This keeps output verifiable and avoids hallucinated institutions.
- One edge function call returns both college and major picks — don't build two separate Groq calls for what's fundamentally one "what fits this student" question.
